       1      in New York State, has evaluated candidates for the

       9      Nominations.

      10             The integrity of our justice system and the

      11      administration and development of law are matters of

      12      paramount concern to our association.

      13             As a result, we have a strong interest in the

      14      process of selecting the members of our state's

      15      highest court, and we appreciate the opportunity to

      16      provide input in that process.

      17             With respect to the present nomination, we

      18      have found Professor Rivera to be well qualified to

      19      serve as an associate judge of the Court of Appeals.

      20             I would like to outline for you the process

      21      by which our association evaluates Court of Appeals

      22      candidates.

      23             We appoint a committee to review judicial

      24      nominations, made up of 17 members from across

      25      New York State.





 

                                                                   21
       1             The rules governing the committee's operation

       2      mandate that every judicial district be represented

       3      on the committee.

       4             Committee members are experienced

       5      practitioners, selected to reflect diversity in

       6      race, ethnicity, gender, and area of practice; and I

       7      might add, include a number of appellate

       8      practitioners.  Their practice settings range from

       9      solo practitioners to large firms.

      10             Upon the announcement by the Commission on

      11      Judicial Nomination of the list of candidates for

      12      appointment to the Court of Appeals, committee's

      13      chair appoints subcommittees to investigate the

      14      qualifications of each candidate, and to make a

      15      report at the meeting of the full committee.

      16             These subcommittees review biographical

      17      material provided by the candidates, read samples of

      18      the candidates' writings, and interview the

      19      candidates' colleagues.

      20             Finally, the subcommittees meet with the

      21      candidates.

      22             Based on the information gathered during the

      23      investigation process, the subcommittees prepare

      24      reports and recommendations concerning the

      25      candidates to present to the full committee.





 

                                                                   22
       1             After the completion of the investigations,

       2      the committee meets as a whole to review the

       3      subcommittee reports concerning the qualifications

       4      of each candidate, and to personally interview the

       5      candidates.

       6             The committee then votes to determine whether

       7      the candidates should be rated "well qualified,"

       8      "qualified," or "not qualified" for appointment to

       9      the Court of Appeals.

      10             In making their evaluations, the committee

      11      members are asked to consider the candidates'

      12      professional ability and experience, character,

      13      temperament, and possession of special qualities

      14      necessary or desirable for the judicial office

      15      sought.

      16             Under the committee's guidelines:

      17             A "qualified" candidate is one who

      18      affirmatively demonstrates qualifications the

      19      committee regards as necessary for judicial office;

      20             A "well qualified" candidate is one who, in

      21      addition, possesses preeminent qualifications for

      22      judicial office.

      23             After being selected as a candidate by the

      24      Commission on Judicial Nomination,

      25      Professor Rivera's qualifications were evaluated by

      12      American University, Washington College of Law,

      13      during which she has taught a variety of courses,

      14      including administrative law, civil procedure,

      15      property, and civil rights.

      17      general for the civil rights, as an administrative

      18      law judge, and as a commissioner of the New York

      19      State Commission on Human Rights.

      20             Additional public service includes, the

      21      New York State Second Department Judicial Screening

      22      Committee, as well as the Advisory Council for the

      23      Housing Part of the New York City Civil Court.
